reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight emerges from a quasi-experimental design comparing teams that adopted variable pricing against those retaining fixed pricing. The primary finding—2.95% increase in ticket sales—is interpreted through a dual lens: first, as a direct consequence of responsive pricing aligning with demand fluctuations; second, as an indirect result of signaling quality to price-sensitive consumers who perceive variable pricing as indicative of high-value events. This duality implies that while the mechanism operates through improved allocation efficiency, it also leverages psychological cues embedded in pricing strategy. The absence of cannibalization in resale markets suggests that variable pricing does not undermine the integrity of the primary market but instead enhances its effectiveness by allowing better segmentation of demand. The breakdown regime occurs when either the unpredictability of demand exceeds the capacity of the pricing algorithm or when resale dynamics begin to dominate the primary market outcome. Thus, the model must account for both deterministic demand-response and stochastic signaling components.
